description: Painted sarcophagus (larnax) fragment from Tholos E, three signs; announced Rapport 1991-1995 p. 422; now published with photo + overall and detail drawings
publication: Sakellarakis & Sapouna-Sakellaraki 1997, Archanes. Minoan Crete in a New Light, vol. I, 330-337 (332)
notes: No reading printed in this rapport; readings appear in Rapport 2001-2005 (three alternatives); item present in silver

description: NEW: silver pin from the Pillar Room of Tholos Tomb B, incised LA inscription along shaft; possibly earlier than LM I; Olivier reads nine signs from the photo p. 333: AB 57-67-41-67-55 and AB 73-01-80-76 (last two signs dotted), each group followed by a divider; both groups previously unattested; parallels: inscribed silver pins KN Zf 31 (Mavrospilio) and PL Zf 1 (Platanos)
publication: Sakellarakis & Sapouna-Sakellaraki 1997, ibid., vol. I, 332-333
notes: Reading printed in rapport (Olivier's, from published photo, in square brackets = his editorial addition); item present in silver

description: NEW: LA inscription incised on the outside walls of a clay basket (large kanistros with two vertical handles) from the east room of the Anemospilia sanctuary; incomplete but 'of particular importance'; nothing legible on the profile drawing fig. 388 per Olivier
publication: Sakellarakis & Sapouna-Sakellaraki 1997, ibid., vol. I, 333 and vol. II, 422-423
pages: vol. I p. 333, vol. II pp. 422-423; rapport p. 189
notes: No reading printed; NOT mentioned again in Rapports 2001-2021; ABSENT from silver - genuine enumeration gap, no reading available from the rapport series

description: Conoid-pyramidal seal ('amulette') from the LM cemetery tholos tomb, cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 423; republished with photo and drawing of the inscription; Papadopoulou continues to call it an amulet
publication: Papadopoulou 1997, in Driessen & Farnoux (eds) La Crete mycenienne (BCH Suppl. 30), 335, fig. 23
notes: ABSENT from silver; Younger (round-1 channel) flags it as likely not an inscription at all; BCH Suppl. on Persee is open

description: Stone libation-table fragment with ten engraved signs, found 1992 by Karetsou; still unpublished at rapport date (to be published by Karetsou, Godart & Olivier)
publication: Status note; cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 423
notes: RESOLVED LATER: published Minos 37-38 (2002-2003 [2006]) with full reading - see Rapport 2001-2005 row; present in silver

description: Small tablet fragment found 1992 by Macdonald; fragment of logogram (?) followed by fragmentary fraction; MM IIA context = oldest LA of Knossos; publication (Macdonald, Driessen, Schoep, Weingarten) announced for Kadmos; notice from Rapport 1991-1995 p. 425 still valid
publication: Status note
notes: RESOLVED LATER: photo published 2000 (Huxley, Cretan Quests); classification discussion (KN 49 vs Wy 49) in Rapport 2001-2005; present in silver

description: Handmade jug bearing four signs forming a complete word on the shoulder, found 1993 by Macdonald; MM IIIB/LM IA; publication (Macdonald & Schoep, Kadmos) announced; notice still valid
publication: Status note; cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 425
notes: RESOLVED LATER: published Macdonald 2000 (Cretan Quests p. 64 fig. 39), read AB 79-53-30-80 per Rapport 2006-2010; present in silver

description: Hood's claimed 'monumental inscription' on shelly-limestone block, surface find 1976; remains of three signs, none truly legible; Hood: LM I?, possibly funerary monument; OLIVIER SKEPTICAL: photo is ca. 1:4 (central vertical stroke ~20 cm x 1 cm, about double the not-small KN Ze 16 signs); plough or mechanical-shovel marks not excluded; awaits technical examination of the engraving
publication: Hood 1997, A Monumental Linear Inscription from Knossos, Kadmos 36, 111-118
notes: DOUBT FLAG: silver INCLUDES KNZe56 although Olivier suspends judgement (possible non-writing); divergence-register candidate

description: Small opisthographic tablet fragment (three signs per side), 1989 excavation east of Kastelli; shown by Vlasakis at the 1991 Cretological congress; to be published with Hallager; notice from Rapport 1991-1995 p. 427 still valid; dating LM IA or IB per Hallager Minoan Roundel I 49 n. 104
publication: Status note
notes: RESOLVED LATER: published Andreadaki-Vlasaki & Hallager 2007 (PDIA 5); texts also printed in Hallager 2008, Colloquium Romanum 359-360; present in silver as sided KH97a/KH97b

site: Malia (east of the east palace magazines)
description: Logogram A 405VAS (truncated-conical two-handled vase) with fraction K inscribed inside it, engraved before firing on the bottom of a small globular jug, found 1989 in a rescue sounding; 'sans aucun doute' MM III; Pelon: A 405VAS cannot depict the jug itself so may symbolise a unit of measure (analysis extended to the vase drawings of bar MA 10); Perna's alternatives (weight of metal vases; syllabograms marking function not type) discussed in fn. 22
publication: Pelon 1995, Empreintes de sceaux et signe incise sur deux tessons de Malia, BCH 119, 584-589
notes: Reading (logogram + fraction) printed; BCH on Persee is open; present in silver

description: Clay disc, surface find, pierced with suspension hole and cut; three rather similar signs of which one, two or all three could be A 344 (possibly related to AB 131); announced Rapport 1991-1995 p. 427, now published
publication: Schoep 1998, A Note on the Inscribed Material of the 1994 Excavations, in MacGillivray, Sackett & Driessen, Excavations at Palaikastro 1994 and 1996, BSA 93, 264-268, pl. 50
notes: Sign identifications tentative (A 344 x1-3); ABSENT from silver - genuine gap; not mentioned again in later rapports

description: Pithos rim from the Bosanquet dumps, graffito inscribed after firing; per Olivier rather a rough sketch of a 'chariot' than the sign AB 87; announced Rapport 1991-1995 p. 427, now published
publication: Schoep 1998, ibid.
notes: DOUBT FLAG (mild): rapport doubts sign identity (chariot sketch vs AB 87); silver includes PKZb23

description: Jar or amphora handle, LM II-IIIA1 (period when LA was only sporadically attested), wine logogram AB 131 engraved after firing; announced Rapport 1991-1995 p. 427, now published
publication: Schoep 1998, ibid.
notes: Reading (AB 131) printed; present in silver

description: Libation table found 1993 (cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 429); text now read complete as AB 01-28-60-04 (hapax) from the photo pl. 133g of Lebessi PAA 1993 [1996]
publication: Lebessi 1993 [1996], PAA, 209-230 (photo pl. 133g)
notes: SUPERSEDED READING: the Muhly & Olivier 2008 edition (Rapport 2006-2010) reads AB 01-09-60-04 (09 dotted) - second sign revised 28 -> 09; present in silver (check which reading silver carries)

description: Fragment of a hollow clay animal (rhyton?) with inscription engraved before firing
publication: Lebessi 1993 [1996], PAA, 229
notes: RESOLVED LATER: full reading in Muhly & Olivier 2008 (Rapport 2006-2010 row); present in silver

description: Pithos fragment engraved before firing, LM IB; three signs read ]AB 188-54-28[ (all three dotted/uncertain)
publication: Floyd 1995, Fragments from Two Pithoi with Linear A Inscriptions from Pseira, Kadmos 34, 39-48
notes: ABSENT from silver (silver has only PS Za 2 / PSI Za 1 for Pseira-Psychro) - genuine gap WITH a (dotted) published reading in hand via this rapport; a_ingestible candidate

description: Second pithos fragment engraved before firing, LM IB; a single fragmentary sign
publication: Floyd 1995, ibid.
notes: ABSENT from silver - gap (single fragmentary sign, no usable reading)

description: 'Selon la rumeur' a vase fragment with the remains of three or four signs; Olivier hopes it will be published under the designation ZA Zb 35 proposed here
publication: Unpublished rumor
notes: RENAMED: Rapport 2001-2005 p. 208 declares the Austin announcement erroneous and renames the item ZA Zb 39 (still inedit there); never published through 2021; ABSENT from silver - 26+ years pending

description: Four signs engraved on the shoulder of a small relief-decorated jar of apparently Cretan origin, found 1992 on the floor of the light-well (room 9) of the House of the Ladies; cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 430 (slightly different terms); see Boulotis's mise au point
publication: Boulotis 1998, Les nouveaux documents en lineaire A d'Akrotiri (Thera): Remarques preliminaires, in Rougemont & Olivier (eds) Recherches recentes en epigraphie creto-mycenienne (BCH 122), 407
notes: RESOLVED LATER: read AB 08-59-06-46 in Rapport 2006-2010 (Boulotis 2008); present in silver; NOTE Karnava's later renumbering would call this Zb 7 (silver has BOTH THEZb6 AND THEZb7 - identity check needed)

description: Fragments of at least two clay tablets (maximum six), found 1992 in space Delta 18a in a lekane together with a sealing; logograms A 302 and/or A 303 (two agricultural products), A 306 (probably OVIS f) and A 54+09 (TELA+SE), the last with at least 200 units; in adjacent Delta 18b ~67 clay sealings of Cretan clay from Cretan seals, some 'look-alikes' of Haghia Triada and Sklavokampos sealings, some with traces of organic ties on the back (lost perishable documents)
publication: Boulotis 1998, ibid., 407-410; logogram photo Doumas PAA 1993 [1996] pl. 113 fig. c
notes: RESOLVED LATER: became THE 7-12 (six fragments) in Rapport 2001-2005/2006-2010 with Boulotis 2008 preliminary publication; silver carries ad-hoc IDs THEfr.1-3 + THEtab.4-5 whose identity with THE 7-12 is UNVERIFIED - identity flag

description: Three joining sherds of local fabrication, final LM IB or LM IB/II transition (later re-dated LM IA per Rapport 2001-2005), three signs engraved before firing: ]AB 56-41-47; first LA inscription found in Anatolia; hapax
publication: Niemeier 1996, A Linear A Inscription from Miletus (MIL Zb 1), Kadmos 35, 87-99; also Niemeier & Niemeier 1999 in Meletemata (Aegaeum 20) II 543-554
notes: Reading printed; present in silver; Troy 'inscriptions' explicitly excluded (fn. 33, cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 431)

description: 'Minoanizing' sherd bearing a graffito of three logograms which could theoretically be either LA or Cretan Hieroglyphic (cf. Rapport 1991-1995 p. 430); now published; new clay analysis relates it to south-Cretan finds, perhaps the Myrtos region (source of both CH and LA)
publication: Oren, Olivier, Goren, Betancourt, Myer & Yellin 1996, A Minoan Graffito from Tel Haror (Negev, Israel), Cretan Studies 5, 91-118; petrography: Day, Oren, Joyner & Quinn 1999 in Meletemata (Aegaeum 20) I 191-196
notes: Script attribution LA-vs-CH left open; present in silver as TELZb1 (Younger alias HAR Zb 1); also cross-referenced from the rapport's CH section 1.2.4

description: Fragment of a large bowl in local limestone found 1987; 'unless it was a stray from an earlier level... tentatively dates to the earlier part of the 12th century BCE'; six signs + two dividers, inscription continuing left and right; two signs fragmentary and unidentifiable, two complete but uncertain, two perfectly readable: AB 01 and AB 09 - compatible with LA, LB, Cypro-Minoan (nos. 4, 44-45) or the classical Cypriot syllabary (ta, se); OLIVIER: the designation LACH Za 1 'generously attributed' is PREMATURE; the 'additional script out of which Linear B directly developed' hypothesis should be dropped; Haror and Lachish inscriptions have almost nothing in common
publication: Finkelberg, Uchitel & Ussishkin 1996, A Linear A Inscription from Tel Lachish (LACH Za 1), Tel Aviv 23, 195-207
notes: DOUBT FLAG: silver INCLUDES LACHZa1 although Olivier rejects the LA attribution as premature (could be any of four scripts; 12th-c. BCE date!); divergence-register candidate
